Linux virtualizing 7 full-speed Windows boxes for gaming.

Hardware passthrough in virtualization is an idea I've been toying with in my head for a long time now. The unfortunate drawback is that you have to be very picky about the hardware you select to do this. Not all mainboards are capable of hardware passthrough, and not all games respond well to being virtualized. Even after you have all the right equipment, it's not easy to set up unless you really understand virtualization. In the end, it's probably easier just to get two machines.

However, if you do your homework and drop your cash the right way it's a great solution for those who would like an instant multiplayer solution in a single box. It's also a neat adventure for the person who loves to tinker with operating systems and hardware. You'll need one video card per person (not all video cards can be used in this way, do the homework!) and a machine with a multi-core CPU (an i7 is a good choice for this) beefy enough to handle multiple instances of a game. I would aim for at least 2 cores per person depending on the game and whether or not it supports multiple cores. The more RAM you have (recommend 12gb+ for 2 users) the better, and SSDs certainly help a lot since you'll be dealing with increased I/O load.

Most importantly, you'll need to figure out what the max draw of all your equipment is going to be so you can get a power supply rated high enough to drive it all. Exceeding your max draw is tricky, because everything may seem fine until you get in to a game, then crashing and instability begins to occur. Remember, a machine sitting at a desktop is not under as much load as a machine playing a game.

I'd strongly suggest anyone considering doing this get a meter for measuring draw in order to confirm that your power supply is good enough for the equipment. If your draw is getting close to the power supply's rated wattage at any point, it's time for a new power supply.
